newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Second Singapore party makes election complaint.
newsitem.headline: Second Singapore party makes election complaint.

text.p: A second Singapore opposition party, the Singapore Democratic Party (SDP), said on Wednesday it had complained to police that laws were broken during general elections last week.
Police were studying the complaints, a police spokesman told Reuters.

SDP leader Chee Soon Juan said one complaint was the same as that made by the Workers' Party -- that Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and other ministers were at polling centres in breach of election laws.
Goh has denied that either he or anyone else in his People's Action Party (PAP), which won all but two of parliament's 83 seats, did anything wrong.
The SDP also alleged that some people had voted twice, although Chee said it impossible to know how many people had done so.
Government ministers have acknowledged that because of a computer malfunction, some people did receive two voter cards.

But they said it was impossible for anyone to vote twice because names were crossed off the election rolls when a ballot paper was handed out. A second visit to the polling station would find the name crossed off, they said.

Chee said the SDP had also complained that in one centre ballot papers were not authenticated by a perforating machine, but were still counted as valid because election officials certified the machine had broken down.
He said no one had told the SDP the perforation machine had broken down.

"We bring all these discrepancies up because...during elections the odds were all stacked against the opposition. We would very much like for election officials, civil servants to be impartial," Chee said.
"These points must be investigated so that in future elections we don't have to worry about the impartiality of those involved in the elections."
The SDP move follows a Workers' Party complaint, apparently not made in writing, against Goh.
Goh replied that he had visited polling stations, but never went inside.
"Nobody has ever accused the PAP of stuffing ballot boxes," he said.

The PAP won the election before a single vote was cast after the opposition contested only 36 seats, but launched a ferocious campaign aimed at keeping the opposition presence in parliament to a minimum.
The SDP ended as the biggest loser with both its seats going to the PAP. Chee himself won only one-third of the vote in the constituency he contested.
